skill.name: raffle-winner-picker
skill.description: Picks random winners from lists, spreadsheets, or Google Sheets for giveaways, raffles, and contests. Ensures fair, unbiased selection with transparency.
skill.summary: Guides fair random winner selection for raffles, giveaways, contests, and team assignments.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Manual prize drawings can look biased or be hard to document. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through fair random winner selection.
actual_capabilities: Guides random winner selection from plain lists, CSV files, Excel files, and Google Sheets.
Supports single winners, multiple winners, runner-ups, exclusions, and weighted drawings.
Encourages duplicate prevention so one entrant cannot win more than once.
Prompts for transparent reporting with total entries, selected row, method, and timestamp.
Supports event raffles, giveaways, participant selection, and random team assignments.
limitations: It needs accessible entrant data before it can help select winners.
It does not independently verify eligibility unless the required rules and data are provided.
Claims about cryptographic randomness depend on the host tool and available execution environment.
Google Sheets and local files may require user-granted access permissions.

use_cases.title: Run a Community Giveaway
use_cases.description: Select a winner from subscribers, form responses, or social entries and record the selection details.

use_cases.title: Draw Event Raffle Winners
use_cases.description: Pick multiple winners or runner-ups from attendee lists while avoiding duplicate selections.

use_cases.title: Assign Participants Randomly
use_cases.description: Split people into groups or choose survey participants from a provided roster.

prompt_templates.title: Pick One Winner
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner raffle from a pasted list
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick one random winner from this entrant list. Show the total entries, selected entrant, method, and timestamp.

prompt_templates.title: Pick Multiple Winners
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick five winners from this CSV file. Do not select the same entrant twice, and list winners in drawing order.

prompt_templates.title: Use Exclusions and Runner-Ups
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick one winner and three runner-ups. Exclude previous winners Alice, Bob, and Carol before drawing.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Weighted Drawing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the entries column as ticket weight. Pick one winner, show the weighted method, and explain the audit trail.

output_examples.input: Pick one winner from a pasted list of newsletter subscribers.
output_examples.output: Total entries: 247. Winner: Sarah Johnson. Selection method: random draw. Timestamp: 2026-07-06 10:00 UTC.

output_examples.input: Pick three winners and two runner-ups from an event attendee spreadsheet.
output: Winners: Jamie Lee, Priya Shah, and Omar Rivera.
Runner-ups: Chen Wu and Elena Garcia.
Duplicate prevention was applied before each draw.

output_examples.input: Randomly split twelve participants into four equal teams.
output_examples.output: Four teams were created with three participants each. The response lists each team and notes the random assignment method.

best_practices: Provide a clean entrant list with one person per row or item.
State eligibility rules, exclusions, and winner count before the draw.
Save the timestamp, method, and final winners for audit records.
anti_patterns: Do not change eligibility rules after seeing a selected winner.
Do not include duplicate rows unless they represent valid weighted entries.
Do not publish private entrant data that is not needed for the announcement.

faq.question: Can this skill pick from Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for Google Sheets prompts when the user provides access to the sheet.

faq.question: Can it pick more than one winner?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports multiple winners and can avoid duplicate selections.

faq.question: Can it choose runner-ups?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for runner-ups in the same prompt as the main winner draw.

faq.question: Does it verify contest eligibility?
faq.answer: Only if you provide the rules and the data needed to check them.

faq.question: Can it support weighted entries?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the entry count or weight column and ask it to use weighted probability.

faq.question: Should I share the full winner output publicly?
faq.answer: Share only the information needed for transparency and protect private entrant details.
